definitions.gloss: penniless; broke; without a cent; flat broke
definitions.explanation: Having no money at all. Literally means not even one mon (an old unit of currency). Used to describe a state of complete financial emptiness.

examples.japanese: {無一文|むいちもん}になってしまった。
{彼|かれ}は{無一文|むいちもん}から{会社|かいしゃ}を{立|た}ち{上|あ}げた。
examples.english: He started the company from nothing.

examples.japanese: ギャンブルに{手|て}を{出|だ}して{無一文|むいちもん}になった{友人|ゆうじん}を{何度|なんど}も{見|み}てきた。
examples.english: I've seen many friends go broke from getting into gambling.

notes:
Composed of {無|む} (without) + {一文|いちもん} (one mon — the smallest old coin denomination). Literally means not having even one mon. The {文|もん} was a very small unit of currency in pre-modern Japan, so the expression emphasizes total poverty.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {無一文|むいちもん}になる (to become penniless)
- {無一文|むいちもん}から{始|はじ}める (to start from nothing)
- {無一文|むいちもん}の{状態|じょうたい} (a state of being penniless)
- {無一文|むいちもん}で{放|ほう}り{出|だ}される (to be thrown out without a penny)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {一文無|いちもんな}し — penniless; an older variant with essentially the same meaning
- {文無|もんな}し — penniless; colloquial variant
- {金欠|きんけつ} — short of cash; more casual and less extreme, implying temporary shortage
- すっからかん — completely broke; very colloquial and emphatic

ETYMOLOGY:
The {文|もん} was the smallest unit of currency during the Edo period. Even one {文|もん} had very little value, so saying someone doesn't have even one emphasizes the completeness of their poverty.
